views.name: sessions_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  CAST(visitorId AS INT64) AS visitor_id,
  userId AS user_id,
  CAST(visitId AS INT64) AS visit_id,
  CAST(visitNumber AS INT64) AS visit_number,
  SAFE_CAST(visitStartTime AS INT64) AS visit_start_time,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_category,
  device.isMobile AS is_mobile,
  device.browser AS browser,
  device.operatingSystem AS operating_system,
  geoNetwork.country AS country,
  geoNetwork.region AS region,
  geoNetwork.city AS city,
  trafficSource.source AS traffic_source,
  trafficSource.medium AS traffic_medium,
  trafficSource.campaign AS traffic_campaign,
  channelGrouping AS channel_grouping,
  socialEngagementType AS social_engagement_type,
  totals.visits AS totals_visits,
  totals.hits AS totals_hits,
  totals.pageviews AS totals_pageviews,
  totals.timeOnSite AS totals_time_on_site,
  totals.bounces AS totals_bounces,
  totals.transactions AS totals_transactions,
  totals.transactionRevenue AS totals_transaction_revenue
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127`

params.description: One-row-per-session facts for Google Analytics sessions: visitor, session identifiers, timestamps, device/geo/traffic attributes and session-level totals (visits, hits, pageviews, time on site, bounces, transactions, transaction revenue).
params.when_to_use: Get session-level detail (one row per session) for analysis or as a building block for session-level aggregations (e.g., sessions per country, avg session duration). | Filter sessions by device, geo, traffic_source, campaign, date, or session properties and then aggregate metrics. | Join to dimensions keyed 1:1 to sessions (e.g., visitor or session metadata) without risk of duplicating session metrics. | Compose higher-level metrics (e.g., conversion rate) by aggregating these session-level measures.
params.output_schema: fullVisitorId: client identifier string from source table (fullVisitorId) | visitor_id: integer-casted visitorId from source (CAST(visitorId AS INT64)) | user_id: user identifier as stored in userId (userId) | visit_id: integer-casted visitId from source (CAST(visitId AS INT64)) | visit_number: integer visitNumber for the visitor in this session (CAST(visitNumber AS INT64)) | visit_start_time: visit start epoch seconds (SAFE_CAST(visitStartTime AS INT64)) | session_date: session date parsed from date string (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) | device_category: device.deviceCategory (e.g., 'desktop', 'mobile') | is_mobile: device.isMobile boolean flag | browser: device.browser string | operating_system: device.operatingSystem string | country: geoNetwork.country string | region: geoNetwork.region string | city: geoNetwork.city string | traffic_source: trafficSource.source string | traffic_medium: trafficSource.medium string | traffic_campaign: trafficSource.campaign string | channel_grouping: channelGrouping string | social_engagement_type: socialEngagementType string | totals_visits: totals.visits (session-level visits count; from totals.visits) | totals_hits: totals.hits (session-level hits count; from totals.hits) | totals_pageviews: totals.pageviews (session-level pageviews; from totals.pageviews) | totals_time_on_site: totals.timeOnSite (session-level total time on site in seconds; from totals.timeOnSite) | totals_bounces: totals.bounces (session-level bounces indicator/count; from totals.bounces) | totals_transactions: totals.transactions (session-level transactions count; from totals.transactions) | totals_transaction_revenue: totals.transactionRevenue (session-level revenue; from totals.transactionRevenue)
params.metric: totals_visits = totals.visits (session-level count; treat as 0/1 per session depending on dataset encoding) | totals_hits = totals.hits (numeric count of hits in the session) | totals_pageviews = totals.pageviews (numeric count of pageviews in the session) | totals_time_on_site = totals.timeOnSite (numeric seconds spent in session) | totals_bounces = totals.bounces (session bounce indicator/count) | totals_transactions = totals.transactions (numeric count of transactions in session) | totals_transaction_revenue = totals.transactionRevenue (numeric revenue associated with session)
params.composition: Safe to join (no duplication) on session-level 1:1 keys: join to dimensions keyed exactly by (fullVisitorId, visitId) or (visitor_id, visit_id) — e.g., join to a session-metadata view that is also one-row-per-session. This view's measures are one-row-per-session so joining 1:1 preserves metrics. | Safe to join on visitor-level 1:1 keys where the other table/view is one-row-per-visitor (visitorId/fullVisitorId) but only if the other side is guaranteed one-row-per-visitor; otherwise you must first aggregate the many-side to visitor-level. Example safe join: sessions_core -> visitor_profile on fullVisitorId when visitor_profile is one-row-per-fullVisitorId. | Do NOT directly join sessions_core to one-to-many children (e.g., hits_exploded, products_exploded, page_views_aggregated if it is one-to-many) without aggregation, because those views explode events/products into multiple rows per session and would multiply session-level metrics (totals_*). Instead: either (a) aggregate the child by (fullVisitorId, visitId) to session-level before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate choosing correct measure semantics (e.g., SUM(child_metric) grouped by session) and avoid summing session totals from sessions_core after the join. | Specific guidance for provided sibling views in the same dataset: | - hits_exploded (NORM): likely one-to-many (multiple hits per session). Do NOT join directly to hits_exploded on (fullVisitorId, visitId) if you plan to SUM totals_* from sessions_core after the join — this will duplicate totals_* by the number of hits. Instead aggregate hits_exploded to session-level (COUNT(*) AS hits_by_exploded) and then join 1:1 to sessions_core or join and re-aggregate carefully. | - products_exploded (NORM): one-to-many per session (multiple products). Same rule — aggregate products_exploded to session-level before joining if you want to preserve sessions_core measures. | - session_rank_by_revenue (RANK): if this sibling is one-row-per-session (ranked sessions), you can safely join on (fullVisitorId, visit_id) because both are one-row-per-session. Confirm its grain before joining. | - page_views_aggregated (AGG): if this is already aggregated to session-level, you may join safely on (fullVisitorId, visitId). If it is per-pageview (one-to-many), aggregate first. | Planner pattern: when composing, prefer either (A) join only to tables/views that are 1:1 with this view on the join keys, or (B) when joining to 1:many, aggregate the many-side to the session grain (fullVisitorId + visitId) before joining so that the join remains cardinality-safe.

views.description: Session-level projection exposing canonical identifiers, timestamps, top-level device/geo/traffic attributes and core totals. Use as a lightweight session catalog for filtering, joining to unnested hit/product CTEs, or aggregations. | Use for: Session counts by date/device/country; Filter sessions by traffic source or campaign; Join to unnested hits/products for hit- or product-level analysis; Compute conversion rate or average session revenue

views.name: hits_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visit_id,
  s.visitNumber AS visit_number,
  s.visitStartTime AS visit_start_time,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_number,
  hit.time AS hit_time,
  hit.hour AS hit_hour,
  hit.minute AS hit_minute,
  hit.type AS hit_type,
  hit.isEntrance AS is_entrance,
  hit.isExit AS is_exit,
  hit.isInteraction AS is_interaction,
  hit.page.pagePath AS page_path,
  hit.page.pageTitle AS page_title,
  hit.page.searchKeyword AS search_keyword,
  hit.eventInfo.eventCategory AS event_category,
  hit.eventInfo.eventAction AS event_action,
  hit.eventInfo.eventLabel AS event_label,
  hit.eventInfo.eventValue AS event_value,
  hit.transaction.transactionId AS hit_transaction_id,
  hit.transaction.transactionRevenue AS hit_transaction_revenue,
  hit.item.itemRevenue AS hit_item_revenue
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit
grain: fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number (one row per hit)

params.description: One-row-per-hit normalized view of Google Analytics session hits: answers hit-level questions about pageviews, events, transactions and timing within a session.
params.when_to_use: Count hits, pageviews, events, or hit-level transactions (revenue) and attribute them to visitors or sessions. | Filter or slice analytics data at the hit level (e.g., find all event hits with a given category/action). | Build session-level aggregates from hit-level data by grouping and aggregating (e.g., sessions with any event, session revenue = sum of hit_transaction_revenue + hit_item_revenue). | Join hit-level attributes to other session- or visitor-level views while preserving hit granularity (when joins are cardinality-safe — see composition).
params.output_schema: fullVisitorId: Visitor identifier from base table `s.fullVisitorId` — the user-level id for the Google Analytics visitor. | visit_id: Session id from base table `s.visitId` (renamed) — identifies the session that contains the hit. | visit_number: Session ordinal for the visitor from `s.visitNumber` — which visit this is for the visitor. | visit_start_time: Session start timestamp (integer seconds) from `s.visitStartTime` — session-level start time. | session_date: Session date parsed from `s.date` via PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) — calendar date of the session. | hit_number: Hit ordinal within the session from `hit.hitNumber` — the one-row-per-hit grain column. | hit_time: Hit time offset from `hit.time` — hit timestamp or offset as provided by the hits record. | hit_hour: Hour of hit from `hit.hour` — hour component for the hit. | hit_minute: Minute of hit from `hit.minute` — minute component for the hit. | hit_type: Hit type from `hit.type` — e.g., 'PAGE', 'EVENT', 'TRANSACTION', etc. | is_entrance: Boolean/flag from `hit.isEntrance` — whether this hit is an entrance to the session. | is_exit: Boolean/flag from `hit.isExit` — whether this hit is an exit from the session. | is_interaction: Boolean/flag from `hit.isInteraction` — whether the hit counts as an interaction. | page_path: Page path from `hit.page.pagePath` — page-level URI for pageview hits (nullable for non-page hits). | page_title: Page title from `hit.page.pageTitle` — page title for pageview hits (nullable otherwise). | search_keyword: On-site search keyword from `hit.page.searchKeyword` — search term if present on page hit. | event_category: Event category from `hit.eventInfo.eventCategory` — event dimension for event hits. | event_action: Event action from `hit.eventInfo.eventAction` — event action for event hits. | event_label: Event label from `hit.eventInfo.eventLabel` — event label for event hits. | event_value: Event value from `hit.eventInfo.eventValue` — numeric event value for event hits. | hit_transaction_id: Transaction id from `hit.transaction.transactionId` — transaction identifier at hit-level for transaction hits. | hit_transaction_revenue: Transaction-level revenue from `hit.transaction.transactionRevenue` — revenue associated with the hit's transaction (nullable). | hit_item_revenue: Item-level revenue from `hit.item.itemRevenue` — item revenue for hits that report item data (nullable).
params.metric: hit_count = COUNT(*) OVER () if aggregated by grouping (representing number of hit rows) — derive by COUNT(1) when aggregating on this view. | pageview_count = SUM(CASE WHEN hit_type = 'PAGE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) — when aggregating by session or visitor, sum this expression to get pageviews. | event_count = SUM(CASE WHEN hit_type = 'EVENT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) — count event hits when grouped. | session_transaction_revenue = SUM(COALESCE(hit_transaction_revenue, 0) + COALESCE(hit_item_revenue, 0)) — when aggregating to session level, sum these hit-level revenues to compute session revenue contributed by hits. | hit_event_value_sum = SUM(COALESCE(event_value, 0)) — sum of event values when grouping.
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE joins (do NOT duplicate hit-level measures): |  - Join to sessions_core on (fullVisitorId, visit_id) — safe because sessions_core is one-row-per-session (same session key). Joining will attach session-level attributes without multiplying hit rows; hit-level measures remain 1:1 with hits. |  - Join to session_rank_by_revenue on (fullVisitorId, visit_id) — safe if session_rank_by_revenue is one-row-per-session; it will not duplicate hit measures because keys are at the session level. |  - Join to page_views_aggregated only when keyed at (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number) or another one-row-per-hit key; otherwise do NOT join directly to aggregated page_views that are one-row-per-page/path without re-aggregation, because it will multiply rows. |  | Joins that will DUPLICATE/INVALIDATE measures unless you re-aggregate first: |  - Do NOT join this view directly to products_exploded (one-to-many: hit -> product items) without re-aggregating products_exploded to the hit level (e.g., sum item revenue per hit) or aggregating hits afterwards. products_exploded is multi-row per hit when multiple items exist; a direct join will multiply hit-level revenue and counts. |  - Do NOT join to any other one-to-many child of hits (e.g., item-level tables) without first reducing the child to one row per (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number) (for example by SUM(itemRevenue) and COUNT(*) per hit). |  | General guidance for composing safely: |  - If you want session-level metrics derived from hits, aggregate hits first: SELECT fullVisitorId, visit_id, SUM(...) AS session_metric FROM hits_exploded GROUP BY fullVisitorId, visit_id; then join to session-level tables. |  - If you must join a one-to-many child to enrich hits, perform the enrichment as a scalar aggregation per hit (GROUP BY fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number) and LEFT JOIN that aggregated result back to hits_exploded on (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number). |  - When joining to visitor-level tables (one-row-per-fullVisitorId), join on fullVisitorId — this is safe because hits_exploded is many-to-one toward visitors (visitor attributes attach to many hits) and will not multiply visitor-level aggregates as long as aggregation is done after the join with care (i.e., aggregate at the hit or session grain as intended).

views.description: One-row-per-hit flattened view: unnests hits while preserving session identifiers and important hit-level fields (page, event, type, timing). Useful for hit-level analytics, first/last page in session, and joining to product-level unnests. | Use for: Sequence of pages within a session (first/last page); Count entrances/exits and pageviews by page; Event counts and event value aggregations; Associate hit-level transactions or items with sessions

views.name: products_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visit_id,
  s.visitNumber AS visit_number,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_number,
  product.productSKU AS product_sku,
  product.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  product.v2ProductCategory AS product_category,
  product.productBrand AS product_brand,
  product.productQuantity AS product_quantity,
  product.productPrice AS product_price,
  product.productRevenue AS product_revenue,
  product.localProductRevenue AS local_product_revenue,
  product.isImpression AS is_impression,
  product.isClick AS is_click,
  product.productListName AS product_list_name,
  product.productListPosition AS product_list_position
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit,
UNNEST(hit.product) AS product
grain: fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number, product_sku (one row per product instance)

params.description: One-row-per-product-instance exploded view of GA sessions.hits.product: answers product-level event/questions within a session/hit (impressions, clicks, per-product revenue/price/quantity and list context).
params.when_to_use: Calculate product-level metrics per session/hit (e.g., total product_revenue by session or by product_sku when aggregated). | Filter or segment by product attributes (product_sku, product_name, product_category, product_brand) at the hit-level. | Analyze merchandising list performance (impression/click counts by product_list_name or product_list_position). | Join to session- or hit-level data (sessions_core, hits_exploded) to add broader session context, provided joins preserve the one-row-per-product grain. | Use as a base to aggregate to user, session, hit, or product SKU level; do not join one-to-many detail without re-aggregation.
params.output_schema: fullVisitorId: GA sessions.fullVisitorId — the anonymized visitor identifier from the base sessions table (s.fullVisitorId). | visit_id: GA sessions.visitId — session identifier from s.visitId (aliased visit_id). | visit_number: GA sessions.visitNumber — ordinal number of the visitor's session (s.visitNumber). | session_date: PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) — session date parsed from s.date (string in YYYYMMDD) into a DATE. | hit_number: hits.hitNumber — the hit sequence number within the session from the unnested hit (hit.hitNumber). | product_sku: product.productSKU — product SKU from the unnested product record (product.productSKU). | product_name: product.v2ProductName — product display/name (product.v2ProductName). | product_category: product.v2ProductCategory — product category string (product.v2ProductCategory). | product_brand: product.productBrand — product brand (product.productBrand). | product_quantity: product.productQuantity — number of units for this product instance as reported in the product payload (product.productQuantity). | product_price: product.productPrice — unit price reported in the product payload (product.productPrice). | product_revenue: product.productRevenue — revenue attributed to this product instance (product.productRevenue). | local_product_revenue: product.localProductRevenue — localized revenue value for this product (product.localProductRevenue). | is_impression: product.isImpression — boolean/flag whether this product row represents an impression (product.isImpression). | is_click: product.isClick — boolean/flag whether this product row represents a click (product.isClick). | product_list_name: product.productListName — merchandising list name context for the product (product.productListName). | product_list_position: product.productListPosition — position of the product in the merchandising list (product.productListPosition).
params.metric: product_revenue = product.productRevenue  -- revenue attributed to this exploded product row as provided by the product payload (do not re-interpret as session revenue without aggregation). | local_product_revenue = product.localProductRevenue  -- localized revenue for this product row from payload. | product_count = COUNT(*) BY <grouping>  -- derived aggregate: count of product rows when GROUP BY fullVisitorId/visit_id/product_sku/… as needed. | sum_product_quantity = SUM(product_quantity) BY <grouping>  -- derived aggregate of product units after grouping. | sum_product_revenue = SUM(product_revenue) BY <grouping>  -- derived aggregate revenue; safe only after grouping at a level that prevents duplication (see composition). | impression_count = SUM(CAST(is_impression AS INT64)) BY <grouping>  -- count of impressions when aggregated. | click_count = SUM(CAST(is_click AS INT64)) BY <grouping>  -- count of clicks when aggregated.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sessions_core on (fullVisitorId, visit_id) — safe because products_exploded is one-row-per-product-instance keyed at (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number, product_sku). sessions_core is session-level (one row per session), so joining on session keys will NOT duplicate product rows or their measures; product-level rows remain unchanged. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hits_exploded on (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number) — safe because hits_exploded is one-row-per-hit and this view is one-row-per-product-per-hit; joining on the hit keys will not multiply product rows (1 product row joins to exactly one hit row). | DO NOT join to page_views_aggregated (or any aggregated-to-pageview or aggregated-to-multi-row dimension) without re-aggregation: page_views_aggregated may be many-to-one relative to the product grain or aggregated at a different grain; joining raw product rows to a one-to-many table will multiply product measures. If you must combine, first aggregate products_exploded up to the same grain as the other view (e.g., session-level) using SUM(product_revenue), SUM(product_quantity), COUNT(*) etc., then join. | DO NOT join directly to any view/table that is one-to-many relative to (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number, product_sku) without either: (a) aggregating that table to the product grain or higher-level grouping to match products_exploded, or (b) aggregating products_exploded before joining. Failure to do so will duplicate product_revenue and other per-product measures. | When composing metrics across joins, preserve measure semantics by aggregating AFTER any join that may introduce multiplicity. Example safe pattern: with p AS (SELECT fullVisitorId, visit_id, product_sku, SUM(product_revenue) AS rev FROM products_exploded GROUP BY fullVisitorId, visit_id, product_sku) JOIN other_agg ON keys — this prevents revenue duplication. | Key uniqueness note: the declared grain is (fullVisitorId, visit_id, hit_number, product_sku) — any join on a strict superset of these keys (e.g., include visit_number/session_date) is safe only if the other side is one-row-per-that-same-key or aggregated to that key.

views.description: One-row-per-product-sale view: unnests hits then products to expose product-level attributes and revenue while retaining session and hit identifiers. Use for top-products, product revenue, and product-level funnel analysis. | Use for: Top products by revenue or quantity; Product-level revenue trends by date or campaign; Analyze product lists and impressions/clicks

views.name: session_rank_by_revenue
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.visitId AS visit_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
  s.totals.transactionRevenue AS transaction_revenue,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) ORDER BY COALESCE(s.totals.transactionRevenue, 0) DESC) AS revenue_rank,
  SUM(COALESCE(s.totals.transactionRevenue, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) ORDER BY COALESCE(s.totals.transactionRevenue, 0) DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue_total
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s
grain: fullVisitorId, visit_id (one row per session with rank within session_date)

params.description: Per-session revenue ranking and running revenue total within each session_date (one row per GA session with rank and cumulative revenue for that day).
params.when_to_use: Find the highest-revenue sessions for a specific date or range of dates (top N sessions by revenue per date). | Compute cumulative daily revenue ordered by session revenue to analyze concentration of revenue within a day. | Join session-level metadata (e.g., user id, session id) to ranked revenue positions for drilldowns and per-session analysis. | Compose with additional session-level attributes (traffic source, device, geo) that are one-row-per-session to filter or segment ranked sessions without inflating measures.
params.output_schema: fullVisitorId: GA client identifier for the user who started the session; derived from s.fullVisitorId in the base table. | visit_id: Session identifier (visitId) cast/aliased as visit_id; derived from s.visitId in the base table. | session_date: Date of the session parsed from the string s.date using PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date); this is the partition key used for ranking and running totals. | transaction_revenue: Per-session transaction revenue value; derived from s.totals.transactionRevenue in the base table (note: may be NULL in source and COALESCE is used in ranking/aggregation to treat NULL as 0). | revenue_rank: Integer rank of the session within session_date ordered by transaction_revenue descending; defined as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY session_date ORDER BY COALESCE(transaction_revenue,0) DESC). | running_revenue_total: Cumulative sum of COALESCE(transaction_revenue,0) over the sessions of the same session_date ordered by descending transaction_revenue; defined as SUM(COALESCE(transaction_revenue,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY session_date ORDER BY COALESCE(transaction_revenue,0) DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
params.metric: transaction_revenue = s.totals.transactionRevenue (session-level raw metric from source; treated with COALESCE(transaction_revenue, 0) when used in window functions) | revenue_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) ORDER BY COALESCE(s.totals.transactionRevenue, 0) DESC) | running_revenue_total = SUM(COALESCE(s.totals.transactionRevenue, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) ORDER BY COALESCE(s.totals.transactionRevenue, 0) DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to session-level or 1:1 session-key dimensions on (fullVisitorId, visit_id) or on (visit_id, session_date) — safe because this view is one row per session (fullVisitorId, visit_id) so measures (transaction_revenue, revenue_rank, running_revenue_total) will not be duplicated. | Safe to join to sibling view sessions_core (SEL) on (fullVisitorId, visit_id) or on visit_id if sessions_core is also one-row-per-session — safe because both are session-grain and preserve row uniqueness. | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views such as hits_exploded (NORM), products_exploded (NORM), or page_views_aggregated if those are multi-row per session, unless you first aggregate the child table back to session-level (for example SUM/recount per (fullVisitorId, visit_id) or per visit_id) or join and then re-aggregate. Joining without re-aggregation will multiply session rows and therefore inflate transaction_revenue, distort revenue_rank semantics, and break the running_revenue_total. | If you need hit- or product-level detail with session_rank_by_revenue, either: (a) aggregate hits/products to one row per (fullVisitorId, visit_id) before joining, or (b) join and then compute metrics using DISTINCT or window/aggregation that groups by the session keys to re-establish one row per session. | When composing across dates, preserve the session_date partitioning used for ranking: any join or filter that changes session_date values for a session (for example, joining to a derived table with a different date assignment) will invalidate the meaning of revenue_rank and running_revenue_total. Keep PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) as the date key for cross-object alignment.

views.description: Ranks sessions by transaction revenue within each session_date (or other partition) to support top-K session queries downstream. Exposes rank and cumulative revenue per partition using window functions. | Use for: Top-N sessions by revenue per day; Cumulative revenue contributed by top sessions; Identify high-value sessions for inspection

views.name: page_views_aggregated
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  session_date,
  page_path,
  COUNT(1) AS pageview_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_entrance THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS entrances,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_exit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS exits,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(fullVisitorId, CAST(visitId AS STRING))) AS sessions_with_page
FROM (
  SELECT
    s.fullVisitorId,
    s.visitId,
    PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
    hit.page.pagePath AS page_path,
    hit.isEntrance AS is_entrance,
    hit.isExit AS is_exit
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_20170127` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit
)
WHERE page_path IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY session_date, page_path
grain: session_date, page_path (one row per page per date with aggregated metrics)

params.description: Daily per-page aggregated web metrics: pageviews, entrances, exits and number of sessions that included the page (one row per session_date + page_path).
params.when_to_use: Get daily page-level totals (pageview count, entrances, exits) for reporting or trend charts. | Compute per-page session reach (sessions_with_page) for conversion funnel analysis or session-scoped KPIs. | As a building block to compute rates (e.g., entrance rate = entrances / sessions_with_page) when composed safely. | Joinable to date or page dimension tables (one row per date+page) for enrichment without duplicating measures.
params.output_schema: session_date: DATE — the parsed session date from s.date (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date)) that groups these metrics. | page_path: STRING — hit.page.pagePath (the page path) used as the page-level grouping key. | pageview_count: INT64 — COUNT(1) over hits for this session_date+page_path (counts raw hit rows that had this page_path). | entrances: INT64 — SUM(CASE WHEN hit.isEntrance THEN 1 ELSE 0 END); number of hits marked as entrances for this session_date+page_path. | exits: INT64 — SUM(CASE WHEN hit.isExit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END); number of hits marked as exits for this session_date+page_path. | sessions_with_page: INT64 — COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(fullVisitorId, CAST(visitId AS STRING))); number of distinct sessions (visitor+visitId) on that date that included at least one hit for this page_path.
params.metric: pageview_count = COUNT(1)  -- counts hit rows after UNNEST(s.hits) where page_path IS NOT NULL, grouped by session_date,page_path | entrances = SUM(CASE WHEN is_entrance THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- counts hits where hit.isEntrance is true for the group | exits = SUM(CASE WHEN is_exit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- counts hits where hit.isExit is true for the group | sessions_with_page = COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(fullVisitorId, CAST(visitId AS STRING)))  -- distinct session identifier per date that had at least one hit for the page_path
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a date dimension on session_date (e.g., date_dim.date = page_views_aggregated.session_date) — safe because page_views_aggregated is already aggregated to one row per session_date+page_path; enriching with one row per date will not duplicate its measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to a page/path dimension keyed on page_path (e.g., page_dim.page_path = page_views_aggregated.page_path) — safe because the dimension is 1:1 or many-to-1 from aggregated rows to dimension, so measures are not multiplied. | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to hits_exploded (or any hits-level table/view) on session_date + page_path, because hits_exploded is one row per hit and will multiply pageview_count, entrances, exits and sessions_with_page unless you re-aggregate after the join. If you must combine, either (a) join keys that are 1:1 from the other table to this view, or (b) join and then GROUP BY session_date,page_path and re-calculate aggregates (e.g., SUM(pageview_count) would be incorrect; instead recompute from hits or use SUM(DISTINCT) patterns carefully). | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join to products_exploded (or any product-level one-to-many per hit) without re-aggregating, because product rows per hit will multiply counts and session distinct counts. | NOT safe without care: joining to sessions_core or session_rank_by_revenue is safe only when those sibling views are one-row-per-session and the join is on a session-level key that preserves the one-row-per-(session_date,page_path) cardinality. Specifically, an equi-join on the concatenated session identifier (fullVisitorId + visitId) would associate aggregated page rows to sessions — but because page_views_aggregated can have multiple page_path rows per session, joining to a one-row-per-session view will duplicate the session-level fields across those page rows (this is expected if you want session attributes repeated per page). This does not duplicate the page-level measures, but it does replicate session attributes for each page row; therefore it is allowed when you intend row-per-page output. | Guidance for composing higher-level measures: when combining this view with other one-to-many datasets, prefer (a) joining to true dimensions (1:1) or (b) aggregating the other dataset to the same grain (session_date + page_path) before joining, or (c) perform joins at a lower grain and re-aggregate to the desired grain to avoid double-counting.

views.description: Aggregated page-level metrics: counts of pageviews, entrances, exits and unique sessions per page_path and session_date. Useful for top pages, trends, and conversion funnels by landing page. | Use for: Top pages by pageviews or entrances; Landing page performance and bounce analysis; Daily pageview trends
